name: mv_rtc_gettime
prose: Precondition: dev is the mv_rtc device with an initialized softc, ts points to a writable struct timespec. Postcondition: the function takes the RTC softc lock (MV_RTC_LOCK, line 258), then loops: read RTC_TIME into val, DELAY(100), read RTC_TIME into val_check, and repeat while the unsigned difference (val_check - val) is greater than 1 (line 268). Because the subtraction is unsigned, a second read that is smaller than the first (for example val_check == val - 1) wraps to a huge value and also makes the loop repeat; the loop exits only when val_check equals val or val + 1. It then releases the lock, stores val_check in ts->tv_sec and 0 in ts->tv_nsec, and returns 0 (the only return statement is at line 276). It takes no references and allocates nothing.
note: armada38x_rtc.c:251-277. Reviewer RIGHT: loop condition at line 268 is unsigned (val_check - val) > 1, not an absolute difference; old prose said 'differ by at most 1' and 'second read of the final pair' was right but the exit condition was misdescribed.

name: fdt_win_process
prose: Precondition: child is a phandle of a device-tree node. Postcondition: loops over the soc_nodes table (entries with a non-NULL compat, line 1808). For each entry it skips the entry when ofw_bus_node_status_okay(child) is 0 or the child is not compatible with that entry's compat string; otherwise it calls fdt_win_process_child(child, &soc_nodes[i], 'reg') and returns that call's result at once if it is nonzero (line 1818). If the loop ends without a nonzero result, including when no entry matched, it returns 0 (line 1821). It handles only the one child passed in, not every node of the tree. The nonzero values come from fdt_win_process_child: ENXIO when fdt_addrsize_cells fails on the parent or when the matching entry has a NULL decode_handler (after the entry's valid_handler, if any, accepted), ENOMEM when the parent's address-cells plus size-cells exceed the local 8-cell reg buffer, EINVAL when OF_getprop of 'reg' returns <= 0 or the entry's valid_handler returns 0 (lines 1832-1855). On success the callee also calls the entry's decode_handler (and the dump handler when MV_DUMP_WIN is set and one exists). It allocates no memory and takes no locks in this function.
note: mv_common.c:1804-1822, callee 1825-1861. Reviewers/mechanical: old prose wrongly said every enabled node was processed (only the single child) and contract omitted values; contract dropped since it reads global soc_nodes. Fixed.

name: fdt_win_setup
prose: Precondition: the device tree is readable. Postcondition: it finds the root node with OF_finddevice('/') and calls panic if that returns -1 (line 1872-1873); it sets the global platform_io_coherent to true when the root is compatible with 'marvell,armada380' (line 1876-1877). It then walks the children of the root, and later of the first simple-bus node and of a nested simple-bus node found under it. For each child it calls fdt_win_process(child) and returns its nonzero result immediately; if the child is compatible with 'marvell,armada-370-pcie' it also calls fdt_win_process_child on each of its children with the PCIe soc_nodes entry and the 'assigned-addresses' property and returns any nonzero result (lines 1886-1902). Returns ENXIO when no simple-bus under the root is found (line 1912); returns 0 when the nested simple-bus search under the first simple-bus finds nothing (line 1923) or when the walk finishes (line 1928). Nonzero values from the child calls are ENXIO, ENOMEM or EINVAL as described for fdt_win_process_child. Side effects of the callees (window decode handlers) are applied to children processed before a failure. No allocation or locking in this function.
note: mv_common.c:1864-1929. Old prose said ENXIO for missing simple-bus only plus a 'processes all' claim; it missed return 0 at line 1923 when no nested simple-bus and the platform_io_coherent side effect. Reviewer (contract bounds) RIGHT for original; contract now empty.

name: tegra_bo_create
prose: Precondition: drm is a DRM device, size is the requested size in bytes, res_bo is a writable output pointer. Postcondition: if size == 0 (size is size_t, so the test size <= 0 only catches 0) it returns -EINVAL with no allocation (line 208-209). Otherwise it mallocs a zeroed tegra_bo with M_WAITOK (cannot return NULL), rounds size up to a page multiple, and calls drm_gem_object_init; on nonzero it frees bo and returns that error (215-218). Then drm_gem_create_mmap_offset; on nonzero it calls drm_gem_object_release, frees bo and returns the error (220-223). Then it stores the result of cdev_pager_allocate in bo->cdev_pager (result not checked) and calls tegra_bo_alloc (allocates the page array, contiguous pages and pager pages); on nonzero it calls tegra_bo_free_object(&bo->gem_obj) and returns that error (229-231). tegra_bo_free_object runs drm_gem_free_mmap_offset, drm_gem_object_release, tegra_bo_destruct, frees bo->m and bo. In that failure path tegra_bo_destruct loops over bo->npages looking up pages in the pager (lines 65-72) even when tegra_bo_alloc failed before pages were inserted, so that cleanup is not shown to be correct for a failure of the contiguous allocation or pager init. On success it sets *res_bo = bo and returns 0 (234-235); *res_bo is not written on any error return.
note: tegra_bo.c:203-236, callees tegra_bo_alloc 177-200, tegra_bo_free_object 81-93, tegra_bo_destruct 49-78. Reviewer RIGHT: the tegra_bo_alloc failure path runs tegra_bo_destruct over pages that may not exist (lines 65-72); old prose claimed full cleanup of 'every partial allocation'. Also -EINVAL only for size==0.

name: tegra_xhci_probe
prose: Precondition: dev is a newbus device with an OFW node. Postcondition: returns ENXIO if ofw_bus_status_okay(dev) is false (line 904-905). Otherwise it calls ofw_bus_search_compatible(dev, compat_data) and checks the ocd_data field of the returned entry (line 907). That helper returns NULL only when its compat argument is NULL; here compat_data is a static non-NULL table ending in a {NULL, 0} entry (tegra_xhci.c:358-362), so when no ocd_str matches the helper returns that terminating entry, whose ocd_data is 0. If ocd_data is nonzero (the matching tegra124-xusb or tegra210-xusb entry) it calls device_set_desc(dev, 'Nvidia Tegra XHCI controller') and returns BUS_PROBE_DEFAULT; otherwise it returns ENXIO (line 911). No other return paths; no memory or locks are touched.
note: tegra_xhci.c:901-912; ofw_bus_subr.c:302-314. Reviewer WRONG (both rounds): the helper returns NULL only for compat == NULL (line 305-306) and otherwise returns the terminator entry (line 313), compat_data terminator at tegra_xhci.c:361; no NULL dereference.

name: rk32xx_start_ap
prose: Precondition: id is the CPU number, node its OFW cpu node, reg points to the first cell of its reg property; it reads and writes the globals running_cpus, psci_mask and pmu_mask. Postcondition, in order: returns false if ofw_bus_node_status_okay(node) is 0 (line 126-127); returns true immediately for id == 0 with no state change (130-131); returns false if running_cpus >= mp_ncpus (133-134); otherwise increments running_cpus (135) and computes mask = 1 << (*reg & 0x0f). Under INVARIANTS only, it prints a warning if the mask already appears in pmu_mask or psci_mask; it does not return false for that. It then reads the 'enable-method' property: if the read length is > 0 and the string equals 'psci', it sets mask in psci_mask first (146), then calls psci_cpu_on(*reg, physical address of mpentry, id); if that does not return PSCI_RETVAL_SUCCESS it prints 'Failed to start CPU' and returns false (so running_cpus and psci_mask have already been updated in that failure case), else returns true. For any other or missing enable-method it sets mask in pmu_mask and returns true (155-156); no PMU start happens in this function.
note: rk32xx_mp.c:120-157. Reviewer 'false on duplicate register' (round orig) WRONG: warning only under INVARIANTS lines 139-143, no return. Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: running_cpus++ (135) and psci_mask |= (146) happen before the psci_cpu_on failure return (148-150); boot CPU sets no mask (130-131).

name: am335x_pwm_config_ecap
prose: Precondition: unit selects an am335x_ecap device, period and duty are signed ints in timer ticks. Postcondition: devclass_get_device(devclass_find(am335x_ecap_driver.name), unit) is tried first and ENXIO is returned if it gives NULL (line 112-114). Then EINVAL is returned if duty > period (signed compare, so a negative duty is not rejected here) or if period == 0 (116-120); no lock is taken and no register is touched on those returns. A negative period is not rejected either (it only fails if duty > period). Otherwise it takes PWM_LOCK on the device softc, reads ECCTL2 and writes it back with the APWM mode, free-run and SYNCO_SEL bits ORed in, writes period - 1 to CAP3, duty to CAP4 and 0 to TSCTR, releases PWM_LOCK and returns 0 (122-139). The function does not check the register writes and has no other return paths.
note: am335x_ecap.c:106-140. Mechanical rejection (contract omitted codes) resolved by dropping the contract: function touches device registers and a lock. Old prose also fine except it implied valid range; negative duty/period pass the checks (lines 116,119).

name: ti_edma3_enable_event_intr
prose: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. This function is compiled only under #ifdef notyet (ti_edma3.c:280-296), so it is absent from a normal build. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS (64) it returns EINVAL without writing any register (286-287). Otherwise it writes 1 << ch to the shadow-region-0 interrupt-enable-set register TI_EDMA3CC_S_IESR(0) when ch < 32, or 1 << (ch - 32) to TI_EDMA3CC_S_IESRH(0) when ch >= 32, and returns 0 (289-294).
note: ti_edma3.c:282-295. Reviewer (contract omits register side effects) RIGHT; contract dropped since it writes device registers. Prose otherwise matches code.

name: ti_edma3_request_dma_ch
prose: Precondition: ch, tccn, eqn are unsigned ints; tccn is not used anywhere in the body. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 (TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (303-304). Otherwise it does read-modify-write on hardware registers: sets bit ch of DRAE(0) (ch < 32) or bit ch-32 of DRAEH(0); in DMAQNUM(ch >> 3) clears the 4-bit field for ch and sets it to (eqn & 7) (only the low 3 bits of eqn are used, line 90); in the PaRAM OPT register for ch clears the TCC field and sets it to ch & 0x3F (the TCC is taken from ch, not from tccn, lines 324-327); then returns 0. No locks are taken.
note: ti_edma3.c:299-330, macros lines 90-96. Reviewer RIGHT that contract omitted side effects; contract dropped. Added eqn&7 masking and ch&0x3F which the old prose omitted.

name: ti_edma3_request_qdma_ch
prose: Precondition: ch, tccn, eqn are unsigned ints; tccn is not used. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS (64, not the QDMA channel count of 8) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (337-338). Otherwise it ORs 1 << ch into QRAE(0) (a 32-bit shift whose result is undefined in C for ch >= 32, and QDMA channels are only 0-7), ORs (eqn & 7) << (ch * 4) into the QDMAQNUM register without first clearing the old field, and clears then sets the TCC field of PaRAM OPT(ch) to ch & 0x3F, then returns 0 (340-356). The range check therefore admits channel numbers 8-63 that do not name a QDMA channel, and for those the shifts act on bits outside the intended fields.
note: ti_edma3.c:333-357, TI_EDMA3_NUM_QDMA_CHS=8 at line 61. Reviewer RIGHT: ch>=32 gives undefined 1<<ch (line 342); also the range check uses the DMA count (337), and QDMAQNUM is OR-ed without clear (347).

name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_manual
prose: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (362-363). Otherwise it writes the event-set bit for ch to the shadow-region-0 register TI_EDMA3CC_S_ESR(0) (1 << ch) when ch < 32, or 1 << (ch - 32) to TI_EDMA3CC_S_ESRH(0), and returns 0 (366-372).
note: ti_edma3.c:360-373. Reviewer RIGHT that the contract omitted the register write; contract dropped.

name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_qdma
prose: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_QDMA_CHS (8) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (378-379). Otherwise it writes 1 << ch to the shadow-region-0 register TI_EDMA3CC_S_QEESR(0) and returns 0 (381-384).
note: ti_edma3.c:376-385; NUM_QDMA_CHS=8 at line 61. Reviewer RIGHT that the contract omitted the QEESR write; contract dropped.

name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_event
prose: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (390-391). Otherwise, in shadow region 0, it writes the bit for ch (1 << ch for ch < 32, 1 << (ch - 32) for ch >= 32) to three registers in this order: SECR (SECRH) to clear the secondary event, EMCR (EMCRH) to clear the event-miss bit, and EESR (EESRH) to set the event-enable bit (395-403). These are write-one-to-act registers, not read-modify-write, so other channels' bits are not affected by the writes; it then returns 0.
note: ti_edma3.c:388-406. Reviewer RIGHT that the contract omitted the register writes; contract dropped. 'cleared'/'set' wording kept qualified; the register semantics (write-1-to-clear/set) are the hardware's, not visible in this file (line 393-394 comment).

name: enable_cpu_feat
prose: Precondition: stage contains only bits in CPU_FEAT_STAGE_MASK (MPASS at line 51, a debug-only assertion); it runs on the current CPU and reads its midr via get_midr(). Postcondition: nothing is returned; it iterates every feature in the cpu_feat_set linker set. For each feature: (1) when stage == CPU_FEAT_EARLY_BOOT and the current CPU id is 0, it fetches the boolean tunable hw.feat.<feat_name> and if present ORs CPU_FEAT_USER_ENABLED or CPU_FEAT_USER_DISABLED into feat_flags (58-70); this happens before the stage test, so it also applies to features of other stages. (2) It then does 'continue' (no further processing and no feat_disabled call) if the feature's stage bits differ from stage (73-74), or if it is CPU_FEAT_SYSTEM scoped and the current CPU id is not 0 (77-79). (3) Otherwise it calls feat_check(feat, midr) if non-NULL, else assumes FEAT_DEFAULT_ENABLE, and jumps to the label next, skipping feat_has_errata and feat_enable, if the status is FEAT_ALWAYS_DISABLE, the user-disabled flag is set, or the status is FEAT_DEFAULT_DISABLE without the user-enabled flag (87-100). (4) Otherwise it starts with ERRATA_NONE, calls feat_has_errata (if non-NULL) and sets ERRATA_AFFECTED when it returns true; if affected and cpu_feat_check_cb is registered, it asks the callback for each listed erratum in order and, on the first result other than ERRATA_UNKNOWN, takes that status and narrows the list to that one erratum (107-133). (5) It calls feat_enable(feat, status, list, count) (not checked for NULL) and sets feat_enabled = true if it returns nonzero (138-140); a zero return leaves feat_enabled unchanged. (6) At label next, if feat_enabled is still false and feat_disabled is non-NULL it calls feat_disabled(feat) (143-144); this runs for features that reached next or finished step 5 but not for those skipped in step 2. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: cpu_feat.c:41-146. Original reviewer RIGHT (system-scope features on CPU != 0 are skipped, line 77-79, no feat_disabled). Round-2 reviewer RIGHT: feat_has_errata only reached after the skip checks (110). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: tunable read at 58-70 precedes the stage skip at 73.

name: cpu_minidumpsys
prose: Precondition: di is the dump device, state supplies dump_bitset and msgbufp; the caller is the kernel dump path (live or panic). The function is named cpu_minidumpsys (the packet name minidump_dump does not exist in this file); it uses the file statics kdh, dumpsize, tmpbuffer, fragsz, dump_va. Steps: it starts retry_count at 0 and at label retry (line 161) increments it, zeroes error and pmapsize and snapshots kva_end = kernel_vm_end. Pass 1 walks va from VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS to kva_end in L2_SIZE steps, adds PAGE_SIZE to pmapsize per step, skips steps where pmap_get_tables fails, and for a 1GB L1 block, 2MB L2 block or an L2 table adds the dumpable pages to state->dump_bitset (a 1GB block also adds 511 extra pages to pmapsize and skips va ahead; L3 pages are added only if in the DMAP range) (176-211). It then computes dumpsize from pmapsize, the msgbuf, dump_avail, the bitmap, one PAGE_SIZE per bitmap page that is in the DMAP range and dumpable (any other bitmap page is removed from the bitmap via vm_page_dump_drop) plus one header page (213-225), calls dumpsys_pb_init, fills mdhdr, calls dump_init_header and dump_start; a nonzero error goes to fail (252-254). It then writes, each followed by goto fail on a nonzero blk_write error: the header page, the msgbuf, the dump_avail page, the bitmap (262-284); then pass 2 over the same va range writing one PAGE_SIZE record per L2 step: a zero page when pmap_get_tables fails, 512 synthesized L3-style pages for a 1GB L1 block, one synthesized page of 512 entries for a 2MB L2 block, otherwise the physical page the L2 entry points to (if it is in the DMAP range and dumpable) or a zero page (288-359); then every page in the bitmap (362-366), then blk_flush and dump_finish (368-374). On success it prints 'Dump complete' and returns 0 (376-377). At fail: a negative error is negated; ENOSPC with retry_count < 5 prints a message and jumps back to retry (rebuilding the bitmap and sizes, so at most 4 re-runs; the bitmap from the failed pass is not cleared), ENOSPC at retry_count >= 5 prints 'Dump failed.', ECANCELED prints 'Dump aborted', E2BIG prints a partition-too-small message, anything else prints the error number; each of these returns the (positive) error (379-399). It takes no locks and allocates no memory; it can leave the dump incomplete on any failure return.
note: minidump_machdep.c:149-400, slice cut the head (function is cpu_minidumpsys; name outside slice was the only reviewer reason, all 4 rounds). Read in full. Old prose said 'physical page for a valid L3 entry' - actually page-directory pass writes the L3 table page the L2 entry points to (351-352).

name: wait_for_aps
prose: Precondition: called on the boot CPU after the application processors have been released; reads the globals aps_started and mp_ncpus. Postcondition: loops with i from 0 while i < 2000 and a local started initially 0 (line 142). Each iteration atomically loads aps_started into nstarted and returns true if nstarted == mp_ncpus - 1 (145-147), before any delay. Otherwise, if nstarted > started it resets i to 0 and records started = nstarted (153-156), then calls DELAY(1000) (157). When i reaches 2000 the loop ends and it returns false (160). Hence DELAY(1000) runs on each iteration that does not return true, including iterations that observed progress; the timeout is about 2000 consecutive iterations without a larger count (roughly two seconds of delay plus loop time), not a fixed total. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: mp_machdep.c:140-161. Round-2 reviewer RIGHT that DELAY runs also after progress (157, outside the if); round-15 reviewer RIGHT that the true-returning iteration does not delay (146-147 before 157); old 'every iteration' wording was wrong.

name: start_cpu_fdt
prose: Precondition: node is a CPU node, reg points to addr_size pcells (1 or 2) holding the CPU's MPIDR, id is unused; reads the globals psci_present, fdt_cpuid, vm_ndomains and cpuid_to_pcpu[]. Postcondition: target_cpu = reg[0], or (reg[0] << 32) | reg[1] when addr_size == 2 (653-657); cpuid is 0 if is_boot_cpu(target_cpu), else the current fdt_cpuid (659-662). If PSCI is absent and cpuid != 0 it returns false when OF_getprop_alloc of 'enable-method' returns <= 0 (671-673), or when that property is not the string 'spin-table' (the property buffer is freed with OF_prop_free before that return, 675-678); otherwise the buffer is freed (680), populate_release_addr is called, and if release_addr is still 0 it prints a message and returns false (681-686; no buffer is held at that point). It then calls start_cpu(cpuid, target_cpu, 0, release_addr) and returns false if that fails (689-690), with fdt_cpuid and the domain data unchanged. On success it increments fdt_cpuid unless the CPU is the boot CPU (695-696), sets domain to 0 if vm_ndomains == 1 or if OF_getencprop of 'numa-node-id' returns <= 0, otherwise to the property value (699-701), stores it in cpuid_to_pcpu[cpuid]->pc_domain, adds cpuid to cpuset_domain[domain] only if domain < MAXMEMDOM (702-704), and returns true (705).
note: mp_machdep.c:645-706. Round-orig reviewer RIGHT (cpuset update conditional, 703). Round-15 reviewer partly RIGHT: buffer is freed at 680 before the release-addr check so the old 'freed with OF_prop_free' on release-addr failure was wrong (it is freed earlier); the 'shorter than four bytes' statement was not shown in this file (only the <=0 test at 700), removed.

name: pmap_kremove_device
prose: Precondition: sva is page-aligned and size a multiple of the page size (both only KASSERT-checked, 2518-2521); every page of [sva, sva+size) has a kernel_pmap entry found by pmap_pte (a NULL result is only KASSERT-checked, 2526, and would be dereferenced by later code in a non-debug kernel); where a mapping is an L2 block, va must be L2_SIZE aligned and at least L2_SIZE bytes must remain; where it is an L3 entry with ATTR_CONTIGUOUS, va must be L3C_SIZE aligned and at least L3C_SIZE bytes must remain (these four conditions are asserted at 2529-2531 and 2549-2552, not checked in a non-debug kernel). Postcondition: nothing is returned. It walks va from sva while size != 0: for a level-2 entry it first invalidates the pending range [sva, va) if va != sva, then clears the entry, invalidates the stage-1 TLB for that page, calls pmap_remove_kernel_l2 under PMAP_LOCK(kernel_pmap) and advances by L2_SIZE, resetting sva to the new va; for a level-3 entry marked contiguous it clears L3C_ENTRIES consecutive entries and advances by L3C_SIZE; for any other level-3 entry it clears that one entry and advances one page; any level other than 2 or 3 reaches __assert_unreachable(). After the loop, if va != sva, the remaining range [sva, va) is invalidated with pmap_s1_invalidate_range. The lock is taken and released only around pmap_remove_kernel_l2 and is not held on return.
note: pmap.c:2512-2574. Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: asserts at 2531 and 2551 require full L2/L3C coverage and alignment (2529, 2549); old prose's 'must have been mapped by pmap_kenter' precondition is not stated in the code and was removed. Unconditional 'on return every mapping has been cleared' qualified.

name: vfp_save_state_switch
prose: Precondition: td is the thread being switched out (KASSERT non-NULL at 595); td->td_pcb is its pcb. Postcondition: returns nothing. It only calls vfp_save_state_common(td, td->td_pcb, false) (597), which does the following inside critical_enter/critical_exit. If CPACR_EL1.FPEN is not CPACR_FPEN_TRAP_NONE (FP access trapped) it goes to done and stores nothing and does not call vfp_disable (519-520). Otherwise (with a KASSERT that PCPU fpcurthread == td) it sets save_sve only when CPACR_EL1.ZEN is TRAP_NONE (SVE enabled) and either td_frame is NULL or the frame's exception class is not EXCP_SVC64 and td_sa.code != (u_int)-1, i.e. the thread is not inside a system call (530-545). If save_sve is true it calls sve_store into pcb_svesaved; because full_save is false it does not call sve_to_vfp_sync, and it does not call vfp_store (548-553), so the VFP registers are then recorded only through the SVE store. If save_sve is false (SVE disabled, or switching inside a system call) it clears PCB_FP_SVEVALID in pcb_fpflags and calls vfp_store into pcb_fpusaved (554-557). In both cases it then does dsb(ish) and vfp_disable() (558-559).
note: vfp.c:593-598 and callee vfp_save_state_common 506-563. Original reviewer RIGHT: early exit for trapped FP (519-520). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: when save_sve is true vfp_store is skipped (548-556); old prose said VFP state is stored in addition to SVE.

name: thunder_pcie_fdt_alloc_resource
prose: Precondition: dev is the ThunderX PCIe host bridge (its softc holds the ranges[] table), child a child device; the function exists only when THUNDERX_PASS_1_1_ERRATA is defined (thunder_pcie_fdt.c:228-301). Postcondition: if (int)ofw_bus_get_node(child) <= 0 it returns thunder_pcie_alloc_resource(dev, child, type, rid, start, end, count, flags) unchanged (242-244). Otherwise, if RMAN_IS_DEFAULT_RANGE(start, end) it returns NULL when device_get_ivars(child) is NULL, maps SYS_RES_IOPORT to SYS_RES_MEMORY in the local type, returns NULL if resource_list_find finds no entry for (type, *rid), and otherwise takes start, end, count from that entry (249-263). If the (possibly remapped) type is SYS_RES_MEMORY it scans ranges[0..MAX_RANGES_TUPLES-1] for the first tuple with start >= phys_base and end < pci_base + size (note: pci_base + size, not phys_base + size, so this is not a containment test of the window in the phys range unless the two bases coincide); for that tuple it subtracts phys_base and adds pci_base to both start and end and stops; if no tuple matches it prints 'Could not map resource' and returns NULL (265-283). Finally it returns bus_generic_alloc_resource(dev, child, type, rid, start, end, count, flags) (the possibly remapped type is passed on); that value is the allocated resource or NULL, and ownership passes to the caller (286-287).
note: thunder_pcie_fdt.c:230-288 (slice cut the head; real name defined at line 230 under #ifdef 228). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: test at 268-270 compares end against pci_base + size while start is compared with phys_base. Old prose said 'no ranges tuple contains the window' which overstated the check.

name: _ATOMIC_CMPSET_IMPL(t, w, s, bar, a, l)
prose: Generated functions atomic_cmpset_{,acq_,rel_}{8,16,32,64}{,_llsc,_lse}(p, cmpval, newval) (macro defined at atomic.h:168-218, instantiated for the three barrier flavours at 284-286 through _ATOMIC_CMPSET). Precondition: p points to a volatile unsigned integer of the given width that is suitably aligned for exclusive/CAS access. Postcondition: the _llsc form loops: load-exclusive (acquire form for acq_) *p, compare with cmpval, and if unequal leave the loop with res = 1 and return 0 without storing; if equal, store-exclusive newval (release form for rel_) and retry the whole load while the store-exclusive reports failure (cbnz back to 1:), so a lost exclusive reservation does not make it return 0; on a successful store it returns 1 (175-187). The _lse form executes a CAS instruction (with acquire/release suffix as selected), compares the value the CAS returned with cmpval and returns 1 if they are equal, else 0 (190-208); on a mismatch *p is not changed by the CAS. The unsuffixed form calls the _lse variant if _ATOMIC_LSE_SUPPORTED is true and otherwise the _llsc variant (210-218); _ATOMIC_LSE_SUPPORTED is the constant 1 when __ARM_FEATURE_ATOMICS or kernel LSE_ATOMICS is defined, the run-time variable lse_supported in a kernel without LSE_ATOMICS, and 0 in userland without __ARM_FEATURE_ATOMICS (68-78). The return value is 1 on success and 0 on mismatch, nothing is allocated and no locks are involved.

name: _ATOMIC_FCMPSET_PROTO(t, bar, _llsc)
prose: Generated functions atomic_fcmpset_{,acq_,rel_}{8,16,32,64}{,_llsc,_lse}(p, cmpval, newval), defined inside _ATOMIC_CMPSET_IMPL (atomic.h:220-271). Precondition: p points to a volatile unsigned integer of the given width, cmpval points to a readable and writable integer of the same width, newval is the replacement. Postcondition: the _llsc form copies *cmpval to a local, does one load-exclusive of *p, and if it differs from the local branches out with res = 1; if equal it does one store-exclusive of newval and leaves res as the store-exclusive status, without retrying (226-236); it then writes the loaded value into *cmpval (237) and returns !res (239). So the result is 1 when the compare matched and the store-exclusive succeeded, 0 on a mismatch, and 0 also when the compare matched but the store-exclusive failed (spurious failure), in which case *cmpval is set to the loaded value, which equals the expected value. The _lse form copies *cmpval into _cmpval and tmp, runs CAS on p with tmp (tmp receives the old value of *p), sets res to 1 if the old value equals _cmpval, writes tmp into *cmpval and returns res (247-260). The unsuffixed form dispatches to the _lse variant when _ATOMIC_LSE_SUPPORTED is true, otherwise to the _llsc variant (263-271). When the result is 1, *p now holds newval; *p is changed only in that case (a failed store-exclusive leaves it unchanged).
note: atomic.h:220-271. Old prose said 'in every case *cmpval is overwritten with the value observed' - true (237, 258) - and 'spurious 0 for llsc' - true (no retry, 231); added that on spurious failure *cmpval equals the old expected value. Name is the macro head as in the file.

name: fpga_open

name: tegra210_hwreset_by_idx
prose: Precondition: sc is an initialized tegra210_car_softc, idx is a reset index, reset selects assert (true) or deassert (false); the caller does not hold the CLKDEV device lock. Postcondition: it takes CLKDEV_DEVICE_LOCK(sc->dev) (910) and releases it before the single return, which is 0 (928-930); no other return exists. (1) If idx == TEGRA210_RST_DFLL_DVCO it does a read-modify-write of DFLL_BASE with the DFLL_BASE_DVFS_DFLL_RESET bit set when reset is true, cleared when false, then reads DFLL_BASE into a local that is not used (911-915). (2) This is a separate if, not an else-if: if idx == TEGRA210_RST_ADSP it writes mask (0x1F << 22) | (1 << 7) to RST_DEV_Y_SET when reset, else to RST_DEV_Y_CLR, and reads that register back into the unused local (916-920); otherwise (every other idx, including TEGRA210_RST_DFLL_DVCO, so the DFLL index also goes through this branch) it computes mask = 1 << (idx % 32) and reset_reg = get_reset_reg(idx), does a read-modify-write of reset_reg setting or clearing mask, and reads it back (921-926). get_reset_reg indexes clk_reset_reg[idx / 32]; its range check is only a KASSERT (842-844), so an idx whose idx/32 is >= nitems(clk_reset_reg) panics on a KASSERT kernel and reads out of bounds otherwise; a negative idx gives a negative idx % 32 and an undefined shift at 922. The ADSP path never calls get_reset_reg. Nothing is allocated.

name: rk_i2s_dai_trigger
prose: Precondition: dev is the rk_i2s device, go is a PCMTRIG_* value, pcm_dir is PCMDIR_PLAY or PCMDIR_REC. Postcondition: returns EINVAL at once, with no register access, if pcm_dir is neither PCMDIR_PLAY nor PCMDIR_REC (467-468). For PCMTRIG_START it read-modify-writes I2S_INTCR setting TXEIE (play) or RXFIE (rec), then writes I2S_XFER with both the TX and RX start bits (471-481); it does not touch play_ptr or rec_ptr and takes no lock. For PCMTRIG_STOP or PCMTRIG_ABORT it read-modify-writes I2S_INTCR clearing TXEIE (play) or RXFIE (rec) (485-490); if both interrupt-enable bits are then clear it writes 0 to I2S_XFER, sets the TXC (play) or RXC (rec) bit in I2S_CLR and busy-waits with DELAY(1) until that bit reads back clear, with no timeout (495-510; the inner EINVAL at 503 is unreachable because pcm_dir was validated at 467); it then, whether or not the transfer was stopped, takes RK_I2S_LOCK, sets sc->play_ptr = 0 for play or sc->rec_ptr = 0 otherwise, and releases the lock (513-518). For any other go value no register is written. In all these cases it returns 0 (522). The INTCR and XFER register accesses are not under the softc lock.

name: vmmops_modinit
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is int vmmops_modinit(int ipinum) at vmm_arm64.c:233-449; ipinum is not used in the body. Precondition: called at module load on arm64, in a context that may sleep (vmem_create/malloc with M_WAITOK, smp_rendezvous). Postcondition: it returns ENXIO with a message if has_hyp() is false (243-247); then ENODEV with 'No vgic found' if vgic_present() is false (249-252); then reads ID_AA64MMFR0_EL1 and, for a PARange field of 4G, prints a message and returns ENXIO (263-265); a 64G field sets vmm_virt_bits = 36 (and vmm_pmap_levels = 2 with 16K pages), any other field sets vmm_virt_bits = 39, with vmm_pmap_levels defaulting to 3 (261-275). Only when not in_vhe() it calls vmmpmap_init and returns ENOMEM if that returns false (278-283). None of these early returns has yet installed the stage-2 hooks. It then installs pmap_clean_stage2_tlbi, pmap_stage2_invalidate_range and pmap_stage2_invalidate_all (287-290; a MPASS asserts the first is NULL). When not in_vhe() it creates the EL2 vmem arena, maps the hypervisor code with vmmpmap_enter (result only MPASS-checked), mallocs a VMM_STACK_SIZE stack per CPU, maps its pages at consecutive L2_SIZE-spaced hyp VAs and fills el2_regs.tcr_el2 (292-341). It sets vmm_max_ipa_bits from the PS field (343-366), builds el2_regs.vtcr_el2 (380-409), runs smp_rendezvous(NULL, arm_setup_vectors, NULL, &el2_regs) on all CPUs (411), and when not in_vhe() adds address ranges to el2_mem_alloc with vmem_add (413-442). It finally calls vgic_init() and vtimer_init() and returns 0 (445-448). Once past the vmmpmap_init check no later path returns an error; allocation failure is not handled (M_WAITOK).

name: vmmpmap_enter
prose: Precondition: pa, va are page aligned and size a multiple of the page size (only KASSERTs, 290-295; there is no check for va+size or pa+size wrapping); in an INVARIANTS kernel each target L3 slot is expected to be 0 (KASSERT at 323 'VA already mapped'; a non-INVARIANTS kernel overwrites an existing entry). Postcondition: it builds an L3 entry template l3e = ATTR_AF | inner-shareable | L3_PAGE with the AP user bit set (reserved-1 at EL2), the default memory attribute index, ATTR_S1_UXN added when prot lacks VM_PROT_EXECUTE and the read-only AP bits added when prot lacks VM_PROT_WRITE (297-309). Then, while size > 0, it calls vmmpmap_l3_table(va) (which allocates missing L2 and L3 table pages with vm_page_alloc_noobj and installs them with atomic_cmpset_64 under vmmpmap_mtx); if that returns NULL it returns false at once (311-314), leaving the pages mapped by earlier iterations in place and any table pages already installed allocated. Otherwise it stores l3e | pa at the L3 slot for va with atomic_store_64 (326) (under vmmpmap_mtx only in an INVARIANTS build, 316-329), and advances va, pa by PAGE_SIZE and reduces size (331-333). It returns true when the loop ends (336); with size == 0 it maps nothing and returns true. No lock is held on return.

name: adadone
prose: Slice cut the head: static void adadone(struct cam_periph *periph, union ccb *done_ccb) is at ata_da.c:2875-3404. Precondition: periph has an ada_softc, done_ccb is a completed ata CCB whose ccb_state & ADA_CCB_TYPE_MASK selects the case; for the BUFFER_IO/TRIM case the caller does not hold the periph lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: returns nothing; it switches on the state. BUFFER_IO and TRIM (2892-2999): lock the periph; if status != CAM_REQ_CMP call adaerror(done_ccb, CAM_RETRY_SELTO, 0): on ERESTART unlock and return with the CCB still owned by the retry, else release a frozen devq, and for a TRIM that failed with an NCQ-trim flag set clear ADA_FLAG_CAN_NCQ_TRIM, re-run adasetdeletemethod and set error = 0 (2920-2926); if status is CAM_REQ_CMP and CAM_DEV_QFRZN is set it panics (2928-2929). It stores error in bp->bio_error, on error sets bio_resid = bio_bcount and BIO_ERROR, otherwise sets bio_resid from adazonedone (BIO_ZONE), 0 (TRIM) or ataio->resid, with BIO_ERROR if bio_resid > 0 for a non-zone bio; decrements outstanding_cmds (setting ADA_FLAG_WAS_OTAG when it reaches 0), calls cam_iosched_bio_complete, xpt_release_ccb, decrements refcount, then for TRIM completes every bio in the trim request after unlocking (error or resid 0 each), otherwise unlocks and calls biodone(bp); adaschedule is called before the unlock in both branches (2981, 2994). RAHEAD (3000-3022): on error, adaerror(done_ccb,0,0) == ERESTART releases the devq freeze and returns; otherwise a frozen devq is released if flagged, then the CCB is released, state set to ADA_STATE_WCACHE, xpt_schedule called and the freeze dropped, then return. WCACHE (3023-3051): on ERESTART it releases the freeze and returns without scheduling anything; otherwise it releases the freeze, then if ADA_FLAG_CAN_LOG and zone_mode != ADA_ZONE_NONE releases the CCB and schedules ADA_STATE_LOGDIR, else calls adaprobedone. LOGDIR, IDDIR, SUP_CAP and ZONE (3052-3396): on CAM_REQ_CMP they parse the returned data into softc fields (log directory length and IDENTIFY-log capability flag; identify-log entries setting CAN_SUPCAP/CAN_ZONE; supported zone mode and zone_flags; zoned info flags and optimal/max zone counts), checking lengths first; otherwise adaerror(done_ccb, CAM_RETRY_SELTO, SF_RETRY_UA|SF_NO_PRINT) is called: ERESTART returns immediately, without freeing ataio->data_ptr, releasing the CCB or releasing a devq freeze; a nonzero other error clears the matching capability flags (LOGDIR: CAN_LOG and CAN_IDLOG; IDDIR: CAN_IDLOG; SUP_CAP: CAN_SUPCAP and the zone support flags; ZONE: CAN_ZONE and ADA_ZONE_FLAG_SET_MASK, the latter applied to softc->flags rather than zone_flags at 3379) and releases a frozen devq. In all non-ERESTART cases the data buffer is freed with free(ataio->data_ptr, M_ATADA); then if error == 0 and the next capability flag is set (IDLOG, SUPCAP, ZONE) the state is advanced, the CCB released and xpt_schedule called, otherwise adaprobedone is called (for ZONE it is the only continuation, 3394). DUMP just returns (3397-3399). Any other type breaks out of the switch to xpt_release_ccb(done_ccb) (3403).

Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: ERESTART in LOGDIR/IDDIR/SUP_CAP (3087-3088, 3173-3174, 3275-3276) and ZONE (3375-3376) returns with no devq release; old prose implied release in all error cases. Round-17 reviewer RIGHT: WCACHE ERESTART releases the freeze and returns without LOGDIR/probedone (3026-3029). Extra finding: line 3379 clears ADA_ZONE_FLAG_SET_MASK from softc->flags, not zone_flags.

name: pmpdone
prose: Precondition: periph is a pmp periph (softc is struct pmp_softc), done_ccb is the completed CCB this driver submitted; the periph lock is held by the CAM done-handling context. Postcondition (ata_pmp.c:580-858; returns nothing): (1) If status != CAM_REQ_CMP it calls cam_periph_error(done_ccb, 0, 0); on ERESTART it returns at once; otherwise it releases a frozen devq if CAM_DEV_QFRZN is set and goes to done (596-607). (2) Otherwise, if softc->restart is set it clears it, releases the CCB, sets state to min(state, PMP_STATE_PM_QUIRKS_1) for the Silicon Image pm_pid values 0x37261095 and 0x38261095 else min(state, PMP_STATE_PRECONFIG), calls xpt_schedule and returns (609-617). (3) Otherwise it switches on softc->state; each of the non-final cases releases the CCB, calls xpt_schedule(periph, priority) and returns: PORTS decodes pm_ports from the result registers, applies the pmp_hide_special adjustments for particular pm_pid values, prints the fan-out port count and moves to PM_QUIRKS_1 (the two SiI3x26 ids) or PRECONFIG (621-664); PM_QUIRKS_1 stores caps and moves to PM_QUIRKS_2 if bit 0 of caps is set, else PRECONFIG (666-677); PM_QUIRKS_2 moves to PM_QUIRKS_3 if bootverbose else PRECONFIG (679-686); PM_QUIRKS_3 prints the GSCR_POLL change and moves to PRECONFIG (688-698); PRECONFIG sets pm_step = 0, state RESET and reset |= ~found (700-706); RESET increments pm_step and when it reaches pm_ports resets it to 0, does cam_freeze_devq and a timed cam_release_devq and sets state CONNECT (707-721); CONNECT is the same with pm_try = 0 and state CHECK (722-737); CHECK decodes the port status: if it shows a live link it creates a path and sends XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS with the SATA revision and caps, sets the port's bit in found and increments pm_step; else it retries (freeze plus timed release, pm_try++) up to 10 times and then clears the bit in found, raises AC_LOST_DEVICE and increments pm_step (738-795); when pm_step >= pm_ports it does a timed devq release if reset & found, sets state CLEAR and pm_step = 0 (796-807); CLEAR increments pm_step and moves to CONFIG at pm_ports (811-819). PMP_STATE_CONFIG does not return: for each port in found it creates a path, sends AC_SENT_BDR if the port is in reset & found, and if PMP_EV_RESCAN is set in events allocates a CCB with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait (on NULL it frees the path and goes to done) and calls xpt_rescan, else frees the path (820-847); the default case also falls out of the switch (848-849). (4) The done tail (851-857) releases the CCB, sets state PMP_STATE_NORMAL, clears events, calls xpt_release_boot(), pmprelease(periph, -1) and cam_periph_release_locked(periph). So the tail runs for an error completion, for CONFIG, and for an unknown state, not for the intermediate states, which re-schedule the periph.

Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: PM_QUIRKS_3 prints (693) and RESET/CONNECT/CHECK/devq freeze+timed release (711-715, 727-731, 773-777, 798-803) were omitted; old prose said the CCB released and periph rescheduled 'in every one of those cases', also wrong for CONFIG (falls to done).

name: camperiphscsisenseerror
prose: Precondition: ccb is a completed XPT_SCSI_IO CCB with sense data on a path that has a periph; *action holds the caller's current action flags (initially SSQ_PRINT_SENSE from cam_periph_error); orig, relsim_flags, timeout and action_string are writable; openings is never touched (cam_periph.c:1646-1859). Postcondition: it returns an int. If the periph has CAM_PERIPH_RECOVERY_INPROG set and ccb is not itself a recovery CCB (cbfcnp != camperiphdone) it only sets error = ERESTART and clears SSQ_PRINT_SENSE in *action; it does not otherwise write *action, *action_string, *relsim_flags, *timeout or *orig, and the CCB is left unchanged (1663-1678). Otherwise it calls scsi_error_action, takes error = err_action & SS_ERRMASK, and the paths then differ: (a) SS_START on a sequential-access device sets *action_string and jumps to the exit with that errno (1696-1701); (b) if the action is SS_START or higher and ccb is a recovery CCB that was a START_STOP_UNIT (for SS_START) or TEST_UNIT_READY (for SS_TUR), err_action is replaced by SS_RETRY|SSQ_DECREMENT_COUNT|EIO and *relsim_flags = RELSIM_RELEASE_AFTER_TIMEOUT, *timeout = 500 are stored (1706-1714); (c) if SSQ_DECREMENT_COUNT is set it decrements retry_count when it is > 0 and the periph is not CAM_PERIPH_INVALID, else sets *action_string 'Retries exhausted' and jumps to the exit with the errno (1721-1728); (d) for SS_START or higher it allocates a recovery CCB with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait, on NULL sets *action_string 'Can't allocate recovery CCB' and jumps to the exit (1731-1740), else clears CAM_DEV_QFRZN on ccb and copies it into the new CCB keeping the new CCB's alloc_flags (1745-1752); (e) the switch on err_action & SS_MASK: SS_NOP sets *action_string 'No recovery action needed' and error = 0; SS_RETRY sets error = ERESTART; SS_FAIL leaves error as the errno from the sense action; SS_START sets CAM_PERIPH_RECOVERY_INPROG and rewrites ccb into a START STOP UNIT command; SS_TUR sets CAM_PERIPH_RECOVERY_INPROG (and RECOVERY_WAIT with retries = 120 when SSQ_MANY is set and RECOVERY_WAIT_FAILED is not, else retries = 1), sets *action_string ('Polling...' or 'Testing device for readiness'), rewrites ccb into TEST UNIT READY and stores *relsim_flags = RELSIM_RELEASE_AFTER_TIMEOUT and *timeout = 500; any other value panics (1755-1837); (f) for SS_START or higher it lowers the CCB priority, sets CAM_DEV_QFREEZE and saved_ccb_ptr = the copy, stores *orig = the copy and sets error = ERESTART (1839-1852). At the exit (all paths of the non-in-progress branch) *action = err_action is stored (1856). A nonzero return other than ERESTART is the errno from the sense action (for example EIO); it can also be 0 when err_action is SS_NOP.

name: cam_periph_mapmem
prose: Precondition: ccb is a CCB owned by the caller, mapinfo is writable; the caller may sleep (M_WAITOK allocations); buffer addresses in the CCB are user addresses. Postcondition (cam_periph.c:806-1000): mapinfo is zeroed first (814). maxmap becomes DFLTPHYS if 0, or maxphys if larger than maxphys (815-818). A switch on func_code builds up to two (pointer, length, direction) buffer descriptors: XPT_DEV_MATCH returns EINVAL if match_buf_len == 0 (821-825), otherwise describes the patterns buffer (if pattern_buf_len > 0, direction out) and matches buffer, and raises maxmap to maxphys (844); XPT_SCSI_IO, XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO, XPT_ATA_IO, XPT_NVME_IO and XPT_NVME_ADMIN return 0 with no work if the direction is CAM_DIR_NONE and EINVAL if the CAM_DATA flags are not CAM_DATA_VADDR, else one buffer; XPT_MMC_IO returns 0 with no work if CAM_DIR_NONE, else two buffers (the mmc_data pointer itself and cmd.data->data, with length cmd.data->len), with no CAM_DATA check; XPT_SMP_IO describes two buffers (request out, response in) with no direction or flag checks; XPT_DEV_ADVINFO returns 0 with no work if bufsiz == 0, else one buffer and maxmap = maxphys; any other func_code returns EINVAL (846-915). It then returns E2BIG, printing a message, if any length exceeds maxmap (923-929). For each buffer it saves the user pointer in mapinfo->orig[i]; for lengths <= periph_mapmem_thresh and func_code != XPT_MMC_IO it mallocs a kernel copy (M_WAITOK), copying the user data in with copyin unless the direction is CAM_DIR_IN (then zeroed); if copyin fails it frees the copy, restores the user pointer and goes to fail (942-955); otherwise it takes a pbuf from pbuf_zone, sets b_iocmd, calls vmapbuf, and on failure frees the pbuf and goes to fail, else stores the mapped b_data into the CCB pointer (961-974). After all buffers it calls BUF_KERNPROC on each mapped pbuf, sets mapinfo->num_bufs_used = numbufs and returns 0 (982-988). At fail, buffers 0..i-1 (those completed before the failing one) are unmapped/freed and their CCB pointers restored to the user values, then it returns EACCES (990-999); mapinfo->num_bufs_used stays 0. On the early EINVAL and E2BIG returns nothing was allocated and no CCB pointer changed. The no-op 0 returns leave num_bufs_used 0 and the CCB untouched. The caller releases a successful mapping with cam_periph_unmapmem.
note: cam_periph.c:806-1000, read in full. Round-1 RIGHT (no-op returns 0 for CAM_DIR_NONE 848/858/868/890 and bufsiz 0 at 900); round-2 RIGHT (DEV_MATCH, SMP_IO, ADVINFO accepted, 820/879/899) and mapinfo is zeroed on entry (814) and left with num_bufs_used 0 on EACCES; round-15 RIGHT (MMC CAM_DIR_NONE no-op at 868-869).

name: cam_periph_unmapmem
prose: Precondition: ccb and mapinfo are the same ones passed to a successful cam_periph_mapmem, with the CCB's func_code, lengths and CCB data pointers not changed (for XPT_MMC_IO the cmd.data pointer must still be valid), unless mapinfo->num_bufs_used is <= 0 (cam_periph.c:1007-1110). Postcondition: if mapinfo->num_bufs_used <= 0 it returns 0 without touching anything (1014-1017). Otherwise it rebuilds the same buffer descriptor list from ccb->ccb_h.func_code (DEV_MATCH, SCSI_IO, CONT_TARGET_IO, ATA_IO, MMC_IO, SMP_IO, NVME_IO, NVME_ADMIN, DEV_ADVINFO); for any other func_code it sets numbufs = 0 and so does nothing and returns 0 (1080-1082; it does not return an error). For each buffer it either (pbuf) calls vunmapbuf and uma_zfree on mapinfo->bp[i], or (malloc copy) if the direction is not CAM_DIR_OUT copies the kernel copy to the saved user address with copyout (recording only the first copyout error, 1094-1100) and then frees the copy; in both cases it sets the CCB pointer back to mapinfo->orig[i] (1106). A copyout failure does not stop the loop, so all remaining buffers are still unmapped, freed and restored. It returns the first nonzero copyout error (typically EFAULT) or 0 (1085-1109). mapinfo->num_bufs_used and the bp/orig arrays are not cleared.

Round-2 WRONG: the loop does not break on copyout failure, only keeps the first error (1097-1101) and continues to free and restore all buffers. Round-15 WRONG: default case sets numbufs = 0 (1080-1081) so it returns 0, not EINVAL (EINVAL is in cam_periph_mapmem).

name: ctl_nvme_check_ooa
prose: Precondition: lun->lun_lock is held by the caller (mtx_assert at 11217, debug-only), pending_io is an NVMe or NVMe-admin I/O (CTL_IO_ASSERT at 11215), *starting_io is NULL or the OOA-queue entry at which to start (ooa_io = *starting_io), aborted_io is writable. Postcondition (ctl.c:11210-11295): *aborted_io is set to NULL first (11219). (1) If pending_io has CTL_FLAG_ABORT it returns CTL_ACTION_PASS, leaving *starting_io unchanged (11226-11227). (2) If *starting_io is non-NULL and its FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_FIRST: if pending_io's FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_SECOND it returns CTL_ACTION_FUSED with *starting_io unchanged (11255-11262); otherwise it marks that first-half I/O with ctl_nvme_set_missing_fused_command, sets *aborted_io to it and falls through to the scan in step 4 (11265-11266). (3) Otherwise, with pending_io's FUSE field: NVME_FUSE_FIRST returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP; NVME_FUSE_SECOND (no matching first half) marks pending_io as missing-fused, sets *aborted_io = pending_io and returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP, in both cases leaving *starting_io unchanged; any other fuse value falls through to the scan (11268-11277). (4) The scan walks the OOA list from ooa_io (including the aborted first half itself, if there was one) via LIST_NEXT looking for an entry whose FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_SECOND; if found it stores it in *starting_io and returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK (11284-11290); if none is found (or ooa_io is NULL) it sets *starting_io = NULL and returns CTL_ACTION_PASS (11293-11294). The lock is neither taken nor released here. So a pending first half only yields SKIP when *starting_io is not itself a first half; when it is, the old first half is aborted and the result is BLOCK or PASS.
note: ctl.c:11210-11295. Orig reviewer RIGHT (FUSED/SKIP/early PASS leave *starting_io unchanged; old prose said so correctly but the BLOCK/PASS description was loose). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the first-half-in-starting_io branch (11249-11266) aborts it and continues to scan, so pending first-half SKIP applies only when starting_io is not a first half.

name: ctl_check_for_blockage
prose: Precondition: pending_io and ooa_io are SCSI I/Os (CTL_IO_ASSERT, debug-only), serialize_row is the serialize-table row for pending_io, lun->be_lun is valid and the caller holds the LUN lock (not asserted here). Postcondition (ctl.c:11698-11795), checks in this order, each returning at once: (1) CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP if both I/Os are CTL_TAG_UNTAGGED, from the same targ_port and initid, and ooa_io has neither CTL_FLAG_ABORT nor CTL_FLAG_STATUS_SENT; (2) CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP_TAG if both are tagged with equal tag_num, same targ_port and initid, and ooa_io has neither flag; (3) CTL_ACTION_PASS if pending_io has CTL_TAG_HEAD_OF_QUEUE; (4) CTL_ACTION_BLOCK if ooa_io is CTL_TAG_ORDERED or CTL_TAG_HEAD_OF_QUEUE; (5) CTL_ACTION_PASS if ooa_io->scsiio.seridx == CTL_SERIDX_INVLD; then a switch on serialize_row[ooa_io->scsiio.seridx]: CTL_SER_PASS returns PASS; CTL_SER_SEQ returns ctl_seq_check(ooa_io, pending_io) when be_lun->serseq != CTL_LUN_SERSEQ_OFF, else falls through to PASS; CTL_SER_EXTENTOPT returns PASS if the queue algorithm field of MODE_CTRL is SCP_QUEUE_ALG_UNRESTRICTED, else falls through to CTL_SER_EXTENT, which returns ctl_extent_check(ooa_io, pending_io, serseq == CTL_LUN_SERSEQ_ON); CTL_SER_BLOCKOPT returns PASS for the unrestricted queue algorithm, else falls through to CTL_SER_BLOCK, which returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK; any other table value reaches __assert_unreachable() (11770-11794). ctl_seq_check returns PASS if ooa_io has CTL_FLAG_SERSEQ_DONE, BLOCK if lba1 + len1 == lba2 (lba/len of ooa_io and pending_io), else PASS (11679-11695). ctl_extent_check first calls ctl_extent_check_unmap(ooa_io, ...): for a non-UNMAP ooa_io that returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP and ctl_extent_check goes on to compare the two LBA ranges with ctl_extent_check_lba (BLOCK if they overlap, else PASS; when the seq flag is true and ooa_io lacks SERSEQ_DONE, ooa_io's range is extended by one block); for an UNMAP ooa_io it returns BLOCK if the unmap data is not yet available (no CTL_FLAG_ALLOCATED or null pointer) or any descriptor overlaps pending_io's range, else PASS (11657-11675, 11624-11654). So the function does not return SKIP itself; the earlier return values depend on the tag and flag tests above.
note: ctl.c:11698-11795, callees 11609-11695. Original reviewer RIGHT (head-of-queue PASS, seridx-invalid PASS, overlap and ordered checks come first as the old text listed them ordered but described ctl_extent_check loosely). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: ctl_extent_check_unmap returning CTL_ACTION_SKIP for a non-UNMAP makes ctl_extent_check fall to ctl_extent_check_lba (11666-11675); old prose said SKIP was returned.

name: ctl_scsi_try_unblock_io
prose: Precondition: lun->lun_lock is held (mtx_assert, debug-only); io is a SCSI I/O; skip says the current blocker no longer counts. If io->io_hdr.blocker is non-NULL, io sits on that blocker's blocked_queue. Postcondition (ctl.c:11862-11955; returns nothing): if io->io_hdr.blocker is NULL it returns at once (11874-11875). Otherwise obio = bio = the blocker, and with skip the check starts at the OOA entry after the blocker (11877-11879). It calls ctl_check_ooa(lun, io, &bio). If that returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK, io stays blocked: when ctl_check_ooa left bio different from obio, io is moved from obio's blocked_queue to bio's blocked_queue and io_hdr.blocker is set to bio, otherwise nothing is changed (11881-11890). For every other action io is first removed from obio's blocked_queue and its blocker set to NULL (11894-11895), then: CTL_ACTION_PASS or CTL_ACTION_SKIP: if io is FROM_OTHER_SC and ha_mode != CTL_HA_MODE_XFER it clears CTL_FLAG_IO_ACTIVE and sends a CTL_MSG_R2R message to the peer, leaving io on the OOA queue (11902-11910); otherwise it looks up the command entry, runs ctl_scsiio_lun_check and on nonzero calls ctl_done(io), else sets CTL_FLAG_IS_WAS_ON_RTR and calls ctl_enqueue_rtr(io) (11918-11925). CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP and CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP_TAG set the overlapped-command or overlapped-tag sense and go to the error code: for a FROM_OTHER_SC io with ha_mode != CTL_HA_MODE_XFER it calls ctl_try_unblock_others(lun, io, TRUE), removes io from the OOA list, copies the sense data into a CTL_MSG_BAD_JUJU message, sends it with M_WAITOK and frees io with ctl_free_io (not ctl_done) (11937-11949); otherwise it calls ctl_done(io) (11952). Any other action value reaches __assert_unreachable().
note: ctl.c:11862-11955 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (BLOCK with unchanged blocker changes nothing, 11883-11890). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the other-SC overlap path frees io with ctl_free_io (11948) rather than ctl_done (11952 is the local path).

name: ctl_isc_mode_sync
prose: Precondition: msg is a received HA message of len bytes, softc is the ctl softc; the caller holds neither softc->ctl_lock nor any lun_lock. Postcondition (ctl.c:1401-1450; returns nothing): if len < offsetof(struct ctl_ha_msg_mode, data[0]) it prints a message, calls ctl_ha_msg_abort(CTL_HA_CHAN_CTL) and returns; the same happens if len < offsetof(struct ctl_ha_msg_mode, data[page_len]) for the message's page_len (1407-1419). Otherwise it takes ctl_lock; if targ_mapped_lun >= ctl_max_luns or the LUN pointer is NULL it releases only ctl_lock and returns (1421-1427); else it takes the lun_lock and drops ctl_lock, and if the LUN has CTL_LUN_DISABLED it releases lun_lock and returns (1428-1433). It scans the LUN's CTL_NUM_MODE_PAGES mode page index for an entry with the same page_code (masked by SMPH_PC_MASK) and subpage; if none matches it releases lun_lock and returns (1434-1443). Otherwise it copies min(the local page_len, msg->mode.page_len) bytes of msg->mode.data into that entry's page_data (1444-1445), computes ctl_get_initindex(&msg->hdr.nexus) and, unless it is (uint32_t)-1, calls ctl_est_ua_all(lun, initidx, CTL_UA_MODE_CHANGE), which takes the sender's initiator index as its 'except' argument, and finally releases lun_lock (1446-1449). Nothing is allocated; page_len is not bounded against the size of msg->mode.data other than by the len check.
note: ctl.c:1401-1450 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (page-not-found return at 1440-1443 and LUN existence is only checked). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: for out-of-range/NULL LUN only ctl_lock is taken and released (1423-1427); lun_lock is taken only after the LUN is found (1428).
